proposals_applied_this_week.reasoning: 9 out of 9 Trap signals expired without resolution (neither T1 nor SL hit). An SL of up to 1.5% away from entry on a 1.5R target means T1 is 2.25% from entry — for an intraday reversal setup that must resolve within the same day, this is a wide move requirement on a stock that just showed a failed breakdown (implying the range is compressed). Tightening TRAP_MAX_SL_PCT to 1.0% forces T1 to be reachable at 1.5% from entry, which is a more realistic intraday move. This also implicitly filters out situations where the trap candle wicked deeply (producing a wide SL), which are the lower-quality trap setups. The 9-expired outcome directly supports that the current geometry is too wide for same-day resolution.
proposals_applied_this_week.expected_impact: Reduces signal count by blocking the wider-SL cases. More importantly, the signals that do pass will have T1 at 1.5% rather than 2.25%, making same-day resolution structurally more likely. Small sample caveat: n=9, all expired — cannot distinguish between 'SL too wide so T1 unreachable' and 'setup just fired in low-volatility market', but the SL tightening is the lower-risk intervention.

structural_proposals.title: Add intraday gap-up as a standalone rally qualifier with its own threshold
structural_proposals.proposed_change: Introduce a constant EXH_GAP_UP_STANDALONE_PCT = 2.0. In the existing OR-gate block that checks had_rally OR had_cumul OR had_gap_up, keep the logic identical but change the gap_up_pct threshold from EXH_GAP_UP_PCT (current value presumably low, since it never fired for any of the 6 missed cases) to EXH_GAP_UP_STANDALONE_PCT = 2.0. This sits at the same position in the gate sequence as the current gap_up check — no structural reordering needed. The idea: a stock that gaps up ≥2% on the day and then shows a blow-off spike candle is a classic exhaustion pattern even if the prior day's close-to-close was flat. This is already in the OR logic conceptually, but the threshold may be too permissive or too strict — making it an explicit named constant allows it to be tuned independently of EXH_GAP_UP_PCT.
structural_proposals.reasoning: GODREJIND (actual_value -0.19%, fell 5.68%) and BATAINDIA (actual_value -1.29%, fell 5.05%) would not be caught even by reducing EXH_PREV_DAY_RALLY_PCT to 3.0%, since their prior-day moves were negative. Both could qualify if they gapped up sufficiently on the signal day — the missed-signal data shows the day_high was significantly above the day_close (5.68% and 5.05% falls respectively), which is consistent with a gap-up open followed by reversal. The existing EXH_GAP_UP_PCT path is the right structural hook; it just needs a standalone named constant so its threshold is independently auditable.
structural_proposals.expected_impact: Potentially recovers 1–2 of the 6 missed signals (specifically the negative prior-day cases). Low incremental noise risk since the gap-up path still requires the full impulse candle and volume spike gates downstream.

structural_proposals.title: Require confirm candle to not exceed the breakout candle's range — relative tightness gate
structural_proposals.proposed_change: Add a new gate immediately after the existing confirm_range_pct < MB_CONFIRM_MAX_RANGE_PCT check. Introduce constant MB_CONFIRM_REL_RANGE_MAX = 0.6. Compute breakout_candle_range_pct = (highs[breakout_bar] - lows[breakout_bar]) / closes[breakout_bar] * 100. Require: confirm_range_pct / breakout_candle_range_pct <= MB_CONFIRM_REL_RANGE_MAX. This means the confirm candle's range must be no more than 60% of the breakout candle's range — ensuring the follow-through bar is genuinely tighter relative to the expansion bar, not just absolutely small. A breakout candle that moved 0.8% and a confirm candle of 0.24% both pass the absolute gate but the relative ratio (0.30) shows real compression; a breakout of 0.15% with confirm of 0.22% also passes the absolute gate but is actually expanding, which the relative check would block.
structural_proposals.reasoning: The current absolute MB_CONFIRM_MAX_RANGE_PCT gate is blind to whether the confirm candle is tighter than the breakout candle or wider. In a 0W/4L market for this panel, the most likely failure mode is false confirmation: a confirm candle that passes the absolute threshold but is proportionally not compressed at all relative to the move. This gate costs nothing on the win side (a genuine calm absorption will always be relatively tight) and blocks the edge cases. No direct gate-block data exists for this specific failure mode since the debug logs don't track it, but the 0% win rate across both directions justifies a structural tightening.
structural_proposals.expected_impact: Estimated 15–25% further reduction in signal count on top of the MB_CONFIRM_MAX_RANGE_PCT tightening. Focuses the panel on only the cleanest absorption setups.

structural_proposals.title: Require reversal candle volume to exceed the trap candle's volume, not just today's average
structural_proposals.proposed_change: Add a new constant TRAP_REVERSAL_VS_TRAP_VOL_MIN = 0.8. After the existing vol_ratio >= TRAP_VOL_RATIO check on the reversal candle, add: reversal_vs_trap_ratio = vols[reversal_bar] / vols[trap_bar]; if reversal_vs_trap_ratio < TRAP_REVERSAL_VS_TRAP_VOL_MIN: _dbg_fail and continue. This gate sits immediately after the existing reversal volume check. Rationale: the trap candle already required TRAP_SPIKE_VOL_RATIO >= 1.3x vs prior average, so it was a high-volume bar. If the reversal candle can't reach at least 80% of that volume, the buying/selling conviction at the reclaim is weaker than the original false breakout — a structurally unfavourable setup. Setting 0.8 (not 1.0) acknowledges that reversals are often slightly quieter than the panic bar.
structural_proposals.reasoning: Bear Trap and Bull Trap combined: 0W/0L/9E across 9 signals (0 resolved either way, all expired). All 9 signals expired without hitting T1 or SL, which is a classic sign of setups firing too early or in the wrong volatility environment. The trap candle requires 1.3x volume, but the reversal candle only needs 1.0x of today's average — meaning a tepid reclaim candle against a high-volume breakdown still fires. Requiring reversal volume to approach the trap candle's own volume ensures the reclaim has comparable force to the original move it's reversing.
structural_proposals.expected_impact: Expected to cut Trap signal count by 25–35% (the 9 expired signals suggest many setups are firing on technically valid but low-conviction reversals). The expired-heavy outcome (9/9 expired, 0 resolved) is particularly consistent with entries that didn't have enough momentum behind the reversal to reach T1 within the day.
